A: In 2025-26 RE, AP's fiscal deficit (4.57% of GSDP) was larger than its revenue deficit (2.33% of GSDP).
R: The fiscal deficit equals the revenue deficit plus net capital spending (capital outlay and net lending less non-debt capital receipts).
x: Both are true: AP's 2025-26 RE fiscal deficit is 4.57% of GSDP against a revenue deficit of 2.33%. R explains A: the fiscal deficit adds capital spending to the revenue gap, so it exceeds the revenue deficit whenever the State invests.

A: The Arjuna Award is the oldest of India's National Sports Awards.
R: The Arjuna Award was instituted in 1961, long before the Dronacharya Award (1985) and the Khel Ratna (1991-92).
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Arjuna Award dates from 1961 and the other national sports awards came decades later, so it is the oldest.

A: On 9 October 2026 the Supreme Court dismissed Andhra Pradesh's appeal, so the 34% BC reservation in its rural local bodies stayed struck down.
x: Both are true: the High Court struck down the 34% BC quota on 1 October 2026 and the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal on 9 October. R explains A: with the 34% BC share, total reservation crossed the 50% ceiling.

A: A tropical rainforest is generally a more stable ecosystem than the tundra.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the rainforest's far more complex food web offers alternative feeding pathways, so it is more stable than the simple tundra.

A: Alauddin Khalji's price controls were enforced mainly in and around Delhi, not uniformly across the whole empire.
R: The controls were meant to keep prices low so that the large standing army stationed at Delhi could be maintained on modest fixed salaries.
x: Both are true. R explains A: since the purpose was to feed and pay the army at the capital, the market regulations were applied mainly to Delhi.

A: Rising interest rates are used to curb demand-pull inflation.
x: Both are true. R explains A: higher interest rates make borrowing costlier and reduce aggregate demand, which is what drives demand-pull inflation.

A: Each bank branch is expected to make at least two Stand-Up India loans.
R: Stand-Up India aims at loans for greenfield enterprises to at least one SC or ST borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the scheme's target of one SC/ST and one woman borrower per branch means at least two loans per branch.

A: The Right to Information is enforceable in India though it is not expressly listed as a Fundamental Right in Part III.
x: Both are true. R explains A: RTI is a statutory right under the RTI Act, 2005, and the courts have read it into Article 19(1)(a), so it is enforceable without being named in Part III.

A: FEMA, 1999 is a civil law concerned with the management of foreign exchange.
R: FEMA treats contraventions as civil offences settled by monetary penalties, unlike FERA, 1973, which treated them as criminal offences.
x: Both are true: FEMA replaced FERA's regulation-and-control approach with management of foreign exchange. R explains A: its violations are civil, not criminal, which is what makes it a civil law.

A: NABARD does not lend short-term crop credit directly to farmers.
x: Both are true. R explains A: NABARD is an apex refinancing institution that refinances State Cooperative Banks, RRBs and commercial banks, which in turn lend to farmers.

A: Direct Seeded Rice reduces methane emissions compared with transplanted, flooded paddy.
R: Flooded paddy fields create anaerobic conditions that produce methane, and DSR avoids continuous flooding.
x: Both are true. R explains A: methane comes from anaerobic decay in standing water, and DSR fields are not kept flooded.

A: Article 325 rules out separate electoral rolls for different religious or caste groups.
R: Article 325 provides one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency and bars exclusion from it on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex.
x: Both are true. R explains A: a single general roll per constituency, with no exclusion on these grounds, leaves no room for separate communal rolls.

A: The deltaic alluvial soils of the Krishna–Godavari deltas are among the most fertile soils of Andhra Pradesh.
R: These soils are renewed by fresh silt deposited by the rivers.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the regular addition of river-borne silt keeps the delta soils rich, making them among the most fertile in the State.

A: Nuclear hazards do not arise only from accidents at nuclear power plants.
x: Both are true. R explains A: improper disposal of radioactive waste is another source, so accidents at plants are not the only cause of nuclear hazards.

A: The NJAC was struck down by a five-judge Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 2015.
x: Both are true (the verdict was 4:1, not unanimous). R explains A: the Court held that executive involvement in the NJAC infringed judicial independence, a part of the Basic Structure.

A: Red sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) has a very restricted natural range.
x: Both are true (it is in CITES Appendix II, not I). R explains A: being endemic to the Seshachalam hills of the southern Eastern Ghats, the species grows naturally only in a small area.

A: The 'Export-Import method' is not a method of measuring national income.
x: Both are true. R explains A: national income is measured only by the product, income and expenditure methods, so no export-import method exists.

A: Acid deposition harms forest trees.
R: Acid deposition leaches calcium and magnesium from forest soils and releases toxic aluminium, which damages tree roots.
x: Both are true. R explains A: acid deposition lowers calcium and magnesium (it does not raise them) and frees aluminium that injures roots, so trees suffer.

A: The Muslim League's nominees to the Interim Government of 1946 included a non-Muslim.
R: The League nominated Jogendra Nath Mandal, a Scheduled Caste leader from Bengal, as one of its five members.
x: Both are true (Mandal, not Ambedkar, held Law). R explains A: Mandal, a Scheduled Caste Hindu, was one of the League's nominees.

A: The Rajamannar Committee recommended greater autonomy for the States.
R: The Committee (1969), set up by the DMK Government of Tamil Nadu, took forward C.N. Annadurai's view that the Union need not control subjects like education and health.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Committee was built on the DMK's demand that the Union shed control over State subjects, so it argued for State autonomy, not Union control.

A: Producers of batteries in India bear extended producer responsibility (EPR) for waste batteries.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022 make producers and importers collect and recycle waste batteries, which is extended producer responsibility.

A: Bank-led self-employment training for rural youth is given through RSETIs, not DDU-GKY.
R: RSETIs are bank-led institutes that train rural people for self-employment, while DDU-GKY gives placement-linked skill training for wage jobs.
x: Both are true. R explains A: self-employment training is the RSETI model, whereas DDU-GKY of the Ministry of Rural Development is placement-linked wage employment training.

A: The Kirti Chakra is India's second highest peacetime gallantry award.
R: The Ashoka Chakra ranks above the Kirti Chakra in the order of peacetime gallantry awards.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime award, so the Kirti Chakra comes second, followed by the Shaurya Chakra.

A: Padhe Bharat aims to build a reading habit among children.
R: Padhe Bharat is a 100-day reading campaign launched in line with NEP 2020.
x: Both are true (Bharat Nirman is not an NEP 2020 scheme). R explains A: as a 100-day reading campaign under NEP 2020, Padhe Bharat is designed to promote reading.

A: Pedakomati Vema Reddi died in 1420 fighting the Velamas.
R: The Velamas of Rachakonda and Devarakonda were long-standing rivals of the Reddis of Kondavidu.
x: Both are true: Pedakomati Vema died fighting the Velamas, not the Bahmanis. R explains A: the long Reddi–Velama rivalry led to the war in which he was killed.

A: Ocean acidification is expected to be most severe in cold polar waters.
x: Both are true. R explains A: carbon dioxide dissolves more readily in cold water, so polar seas absorb more and acidify most.

A: Kolattam is a group dance in which the dancers beat sticks in rhythm.
x: Both are true (Kolattam was the main dance of the Eastern Chalukya era, not the Kakatiya). R explains A: it is a stick dance by a group of 8 or 12 dancers led by a Pennadi.

A: The Public Service Commission of British India was set up in 1926, after the Lee Commission reported.
R: The Lee Commission (1924) recommended setting up an independent Public Service Commission.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Commission was created in 1926 on the Lee Commission's 1924 recommendation.

A: The Thirteenth Schedule only asks for the feasibility of a SAIL steel plant in YSR district to be examined.
x: Both are true. R explains A: only the new major port carries 'shall develop'; the steel plant, refinery, railway zone and VCIC are only to be 'examined'.

A: The Vande Mataram Coastal Cyclothon 2026 marked the 150th anniversary of Vande Mataram.
R: Vande Mataram was written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in 1875.
x: Both are true (the AP leg ended at Naidupeta, not Koppili). R explains A: a song written in 1875 completes 150 years in 2025-26, which the Cyclothon celebrated.

A: Farmers can avoid distress sale of their harvest by taking loans against warehouse receipts.
x: Both are true (the Kisan Rin Portal integrates KCC and interest subvention data, not Soil Health Cards). R explains A: post-harvest loans at 7% for up to six months against WDRA receipts let farmers store and sell later.

A: Qatar has been designated a Major Non-NATO Ally of the US (2022).
R: Qatar hosts the Al-Udeid Air Base, the largest US base in the Middle East, and is a close US security partner.
x: Both are true: Qatar became an MNNA in 2022, not 2020. R explains A: its role as host of the largest US base in the region underpins the designation.

A: Amaravati is one of the Buddhist circuit sites of Andhra Pradesh.
R: Amaravati was a major Buddhist centre, with the Mahachaitya (great stupa) of the Satavahana-Ikshvaku age.
x: Both are true (Srisailam is a Shaiva site, not a Buddhist one). R explains A: Amaravati's great stupa makes it a key stop on the Buddhist circuit.

A: After the 44th Amendment, a National Emergency cannot be proclaimed on the oral advice of the Prime Minister alone.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the 44th Amendment requires the written recommendation of the Cabinet, so the Prime Minister's oral advice is not enough.

A: India plans about 97 GW of new coal-based capacity by 2035 despite its renewable push.
R: CEA and CERC see this capacity as needed for grid stability, with 70 GW in renewable-rich States.
x: Both are true (the plants are to run till 2050, not retire by 2040). R explains A: the new coal capacity is planned to balance variable renewable power and keep the grid stable.

A: Directive Principles, though non-justiciable, are used in constitutional interpretation.
x: Both are true. R explains A: reading Article 45 with Article 21 led to the right to education and Article 21A (86th Amendment, 2002), showing DPSPs guide interpretation.

A: India now has a single synchronous national power grid.
R: The Southern Grid was synchronised with the rest of the national grid in December 2013.
x: Both are true: the five regional grids now work as one (One Nation, One Grid). R explains A: the Southern Grid's synchronisation in December 2013 completed the single national grid.

A: Sagarmala aims at the welfare of coastal communities besides port development.
x: Both are true (Dedicated Freight Corridors are not a Sagarmala pillar). R explains A: coastal community development is one of Sagarmala's pillars.

A: Banda Bahadur was executed at Delhi in 1716 on the orders of Farrukhsiyar.
R: Banda Bahadur, captured at Gurdas Nangal, refused to convert to Islam.
x: Both are true: Aurangzeb had died in 1707, so it was Farrukhsiyar who ordered the execution. R explains A: Banda was put to death after refusing to convert.

A: Deforestation contributes to global warming.
x: Both are true (the highest forest loss is in the tropics, not temperate Europe and North America). R explains A: deforestation reduces the carbon sink and adds to the greenhouse effect.

A: Advertising a drug as a 'magic remedy' to cure a disease listed in the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act, 1954 is an offence.
x: Both are true (the Act does not ban the sale of generic medicines). R explains A: the Act prohibits the publication of objectionable advertisements of drugs claiming magic cures.

A: The Red Sea separates Africa from the Arabian Peninsula of Asia.
x: Both are true (the Red Sea is not associated with Europe). R explains A: it is an axial trough between Africa and Arabia, part of the Great Rift system.

A: The Ministry of Home Affairs is the nodal ministry for civil defence in India.
R: Civil defence is governed by the Civil Defence Act, 1968, which the MHA administers.
x: Both are true (the Civil Defence Volunteer Force was announced on the 80th Independence Day, 2026, not the 79th). R explains A: the MHA administers the Civil Defence Act, 1968.

A: FDI in defence above 74% needs government approval.
R: FDI in defence up to 74% is permitted through the automatic route, and beyond that through the government route.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the automatic route stops at 74%, so higher FDI in defence requires government approval.

A: The average growth of Andhra Pradesh's agriculture and allied sector since bifurcation (to 2018) was well below 18%.
x: Both are true. R explains A: 18.23% in 2017-18 was the single-year peak, so the average over all the years was lower.

A: A State Human Rights Commission cannot inquire into human rights violations relating to subjects in the Union List.
x: Both are true. R explains A: an SHRC inquires only into matters in the State List and the Concurrent List, so Union List subjects are outside it.

A: India's Look East Policy was formulated under P.V. Narasimha Rao.
R: The Look East Policy was launched in 1991-92, when P.V. Narasimha Rao was Prime Minister.
x: Both are true (it was not formulated by Vajpayee; Modi upgraded it to Act East in 2014). R explains A: it was launched during Narasimha Rao's term.

A: Nagaland has no Sixth Schedule autonomous district councils.
R: Under Article 244(2) the Sixth Schedule applies only to tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
x: Both are true. R explains A: Nagaland is not among the four Sixth Schedule States (it has Article 371A instead).

A: Communal riots often lead to ghettoisation in mixed neighbourhoods.
R: Fear after riots pushes communities into religiously segregated neighbourhoods, which is ghettoisation.
x: Both are true (riots weaken, not strengthen, social capital). R explains A: insecurity after riots drives families into segregated localities.

A: Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, farmers who repay promptly effectively pay 4% interest on short-term loans.
x: Both are true. R explains A: loans are given at 7%, and the 3% prompt repayment incentive brings the effective rate down to 4%.

A: Under the Supreme Court's triple test, an OBC quota in local bodies that takes total reservation above 50 per cent is invalid.
x: Both are true (the test needs a dedicated commission, not NCBC approval). R explains A: the triple test requires total reservation in local bodies to stay within 50 per cent.

A: The 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit marked 25 years of the India-Russia strategic partnership.
R: The India-Russia Declaration on Strategic Partnership was signed in October 2000.
x: Both are true (Russia is not in I2U2, which is India, Israel, UAE and US). R explains A: a partnership signed in 2000 completed 25 years at the 2025 summit.

A: The east coast of India is largely an emergent coast.
R: The east coast has been raised relative to the sea and has a wide continental shelf, beaches, bars, lagoons and deltas.
x: Both are true (the east coast is emergent, not submergent). R explains A: uplift relative to sea level and the resulting wide shelf and depositional features are what make a coast emergent.

A: Rand and Ayerst were killed by the Chapekar brothers in 1897, during the viceroyalty of Elgin II.
R: Rand headed the Pune Plague Committee, whose harsh search-and-segregation measures angered the people.
x: Both are true: the killing was in 1897 under Elgin II, not Minto II. R explains A: the Chapekars shot Rand over the high-handed plague measures.

A: Submarine-launched missiles are regarded as the most survivable leg of India's nuclear triad.
x: Both are true (land-based missiles are easier to detect). R explains A: SSBNs stay concealed under the sea, giving a sure second-strike capability.

A: A rocket can move forward in the vacuum of space.
R: A rocket works on Newton's third law: the gases it expels push it forward without any surrounding air.
x: Both are true (a rocket does not need air to push against). R explains A: action and reaction act between the rocket and its exhaust, so it works in a vacuum.

A: The Street Lighting National Programme replaces conventional street lights with LED lights.
R: The LED is far more energy-efficient than sodium vapour and other conventional lamps.
x: Both are true (SLNP replaces sodium lamps with LEDs, not the reverse). R explains A: LEDs save energy, which is the purpose of the programme.

A: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary is known mainly for its mangroves.
x: Both are true (Coringa has no coral reefs or dugongs). R explains A: Coringa protects the mangroves of the Godavari estuary.

A: The T.K. Viswanathan Committee of 2015 is linked to India's insolvency law.
x: Both are true (it was not a SEBI committee on fair market conduct). R explains A: the 2015 Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee chaired by Viswanathan formed the basis of the IBC, 2016.

A: The 16th Finance Commission did not raise the States' share in the divisible pool above 41%.
R: The 16th Finance Commission retained the 41% share recommended by the 15th Finance Commission for 2026-31.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the share was kept at the 15th FC's level of 41%, so it was not raised.

A: The UP Cabinet's decision of 9 October 2026 could not by itself rename the Noida (Jewar) airport.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the final decision on naming an airport rests with the Union Cabinet followed by a Gazette notification, so a State Cabinet decision is only a proposal.

A: Indira Jaising is known for her work on women's rights law.
x: Both are true (in 2009 she became the first woman Additional Solicitor General, not Solicitor General). R explains A: she helped shape the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

A: The Governor of Andhra Pradesh can no longer nominate an Anglo-Indian member to the State Assembly.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the 104th Amendment (2020) ended the nomination of Anglo-Indians under Article 333, so Section 18 of the AP Reorganisation Act no longer operates.

A: Less developed countries generally lose more lives to disasters than developed ones.
R: Low development means weak buildings, warning systems and preparedness, which raises vulnerability to disasters.
x: Both are true (higher development lowers, not raises, the death toll). R explains A: poor preparedness and infrastructure make the same hazard deadlier in poorer countries.

A: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation helped free tribals from exploitation by moneylenders.
x: Both are true (the GCC was set up in 1956, before the Srikakulam movement). R explains A: by buying minor forest produce and supplying essentials, the GCC freed tribals from moneylenders.

A: The Haryana State Employment of Local Candidates Act, 2020 was struck down by the Punjab and Haryana High Court in November 2023.
x: Both are true: it was the High Court, not the Supreme Court. R explains A: the court found the local job quota contrary to Articles 14, 15, 16 and 19.

A: The headquarters of the IMF is at Washington, D.C.
x: Both are true (it is not at New York). R explains A: the IMF and IBRD, the Bretton Woods twins, are both headquartered at Washington, D.C.

A: The Nepal flood of August 2026 was not a conventional glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF).
x: Both are true. R explains A: the flood came from an ice-rock avalanche off Mt Langtang Lirung that choked the Lhende River, a debris flood rather than a burst glacial lake.

A: Telugu and Muslim sources differ on the number of times Warangal was invaded.
R: Telugu sources count eight invasions of Warangal, while Muslim sources such as Amir Khusrau and Wassaf count five.
x: Both are true (the sources do not agree on five). R explains A: the counts of eight and five show the disagreement.

A: Under PAT, energy-intensive units that beat their targets earn tradable Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts).
x: Both are true (PAT gives ESCerts, not carbon credits). R explains A: PAT is a market mechanism under NMEEE in which surplus savings are certified and traded.

A: Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam became part of India de jure only in 1962.
R: France ratified the 1956 Treaty of Cession only in 1962.
x: Both are true: the transfer was de facto in 1954 and de jure in 1962. R explains A: legal transfer took effect when France ratified the treaty in 1962.

A: Exogamy is the rule of marrying outside one's own group, such as the gotra or clan.
x: Both are true (marrying within the group is endogamy). R explains A: the incest taboo forbidding relations among close kin is the basis of marrying outside the group.

A: Offences under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 are non-compoundable.
R: Section 8 of the Act, as amended, makes every offence under it non-bailable and non-compoundable.
x: Both are true (dowry offences are not compoundable). R explains A: Section 8 expressly declares them non-compoundable.

A: Replacing enforceable welfare rights with discretionary transfers weakens the position of welfare beneficiaries.
x: Both are true. R explains A: discretionary transfers turn rights-holders into passive beneficiaries who cannot claim them, weakening their position.

A: Germanwatch is the publisher of the Climate Change Performance Index.
x: Both are true (the Environmental Performance Index is by Yale and Columbia). R explains A: Germanwatch publishes the CCPI and the Climate Risk Index.

A: The State Legislative Assembly is not necessarily dissolved when President's Rule is imposed.
R: During President's Rule the Assembly may be kept in suspended animation while its powers are exercisable by or under the authority of Parliament (Article 357).
x: Both are true. R explains A: since Parliament takes over the legislature's powers, the Assembly can simply be suspended rather than dissolved.

A: The mihrab marks the direction of prayer in a mosque.
R: The mihrab is a niche in the qibla wall, which faces Mecca.
x: Both are true (the pulpit is the minbar, not the mihrab). R explains A: being set in the qibla wall, the mihrab shows worshippers the direction of Mecca.

A: The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor.
R: Under Article 165 the Governor appoints the Advocate General, who holds office during the Governor's pleasure.
x: Both are true (the President has no role). R explains A: Article 165 vests the appointment in the Governor.

A: The Great Nicobar Project has raised concerns over the Giant Leatherback Turtle.
x: Both are true (the NGT did not cancel the project's clearance). R explains A: Galathea Bay, the site of the transshipment terminal, is a nesting site of the leatherback.

A: A State Legislative Council can be created or abolished without a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
x: Both are true. R explains A: under Article 169 Parliament does it by ordinary law after the Assembly's special-majority resolution, and such a law is not deemed an Article 368 amendment.

A: The Serious Fraud Investigation Office functions under the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.
R: The SFIO is a statutory body under Section 211 of the Companies Act, 2013, which the Ministry of Corporate Affairs administers.
x: Both are true (it is not under the Finance Ministry). R explains A: the SFIO is created under the Companies Act, administered by the MCA.

A: NITI Aayog oversees the SDG India Index.
x: Both are true (the National Indicator Framework is developed by MoSPI, not NITI Aayog). R explains A: as the SDG coordinating body, NITI Aayog prepares the SDG India Index.

A: SEBI has quasi-judicial powers.
x: Both are true (SEBI is not merely advisory). R explains A: SEBI can investigate, summon, pass orders and impose penalties, which are quasi-judicial functions.

A: Mahendragiri does not belong to the Western (Rayalaseema) plateau of Andhra Pradesh.
R: Mahendragiri belongs to the Eastern Ghats hill region of north Andhra (Srikakulam).
x: Both are true. R explains A: Mahendragiri lies in the north-eastern Eastern Ghats hill region, far from the Rayalaseema plateau.

A: A higher fiscal deficit tends to widen the current account deficit.
R: Government dissaving reduces national savings, and the current account deficit equals the gap between investment and national savings.
x: Both are true (it widens, not narrows, the CAD - the twin deficits). R explains A: lower national savings with the same investment means a larger CAD.

A: Bharat Rice (February 2024) was launched to give consumers rice at a subsidised price.
R: Bharat-brand rice is sold at a fixed low price of ₹29 a kg through NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar outlets.
x: Both are true (it did not replace MSP procurement). R explains A: the low fixed price through these outlets is how it gives consumers cheap rice.

A: Pataliputra had declined by the time Hiuen-Tsang came.
x: Both are true (it was no longer the largest city). R explains A: R.S. Sharma's urban decay thesis shows towns shrinking in the post-Gupta period, which explains Pataliputra's decline.

A: Quantum tunnelling, the phenomenon behind the Physics Nobel 2025, also makes nuclear fusion in the Sun possible.
R: Tunnelling lets protons in the Sun's core cross the electrical repulsion barrier between them and fuse.
x: Both are true (fusion is not an application of the prize-winning circuit work, but the same phenomenon in nature). R explains A: without tunnelling the Sun's core is not hot enough for protons to fuse.

A: Under AP's 3% sports quota, APPSC recruits from a merit list it does not itself prepare.
x: Both are true (no APPSC written examination is the basis). R explains A: the merit list is prepared by a State Level Committee and APPSC and other boards recruit from it.

A: The Scarce Rainfall Zone receives the lowest rainfall in Andhra Pradesh.
R: Kurnool and Anantapuramu lie in the rain-shadow region, away from the main paths of both monsoons.
x: Both are true (it gets the lowest, not the highest rainfall). R explains A: the rain-shadow location is why this zone receives so little rain.

A: Mutation of land records does not confer title to land.
R: Mutation entries serve only fiscal purposes, mainly the collection of land revenue.
x: Both are true. R explains A: as courts have held, mutation is only a revenue record, so it creates no title.

A: The Zonal Councils are statutory bodies set up under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956.
R: Part III of the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 created five Zonal Councils.
x: Both are true (they are not constitutional bodies or created by the 7th Amendment). R explains A: they owe their existence to the SRA, 1956, a statute.

A: The Yashasvini Campaign aims to empower women entrepreneurs.
x: Both are true (the ODR Portal is for delayed MSME payments, not women MSMEs). R explains A: Yashasvini focuses on women-owned MSMEs.

A: The 1323 conquest of Warangal was led by Ulugh Khan (later Muhammad bin Tughluq).
R: Ulugh Khan, sent by Ghiyasuddin Tughluq, annexed the Kakatiya kingdom after a second siege of Warangal.
x: Both are true: Khusrau Khan led the 1318 expedition, not 1323. R explains A: Ulugh Khan was the commander who took Warangal in 1323.

A: Pollen grains in the air are a natural cause of air pollution.
x: Both are true (pollen is natural, not anthropogenic). R explains A: natural causes of air pollution include forest fires, volcanoes, dust storms and pollen.

A: Credit for the 2016 equalisation levy could not be claimed under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the levy was outside the Income Tax Act, so it was not an income tax covered by DTAAs.

A: The Supreme Court held that the right to walk on footpaths is a fundamental right under Articles 19(1)(d) and 21.
R: Safe movement on public roads is part of the freedom to move throughout India and of the right to life with dignity.
x: Both are true (the Articles are 19(1)(d) and 21, not 20). R explains A: free and safe movement is part of these two rights.

A: The Polavaram-Nallamala Sagar Link aims to drought-proof Rayalaseema.
x: Both are true (the link serves Rayalaseema, not North Coastal Andhra). R explains A: it carries surplus Godavari floodwater to Rayalaseema.

A: The second India-Pakistan war over Kashmir was fought in 1965.
x: Both are true (the first was in 1947-48). R explains A: the 1965 war followed Pakistan's Operation Gibraltar and Operation Grand Slam in Kashmir.

A: In PLFS 2023-24, Andhra Pradesh's unemployment rate was above the national rate.
R: Andhra Pradesh has high urban and youth unemployment.
x: Both are true (AP's female rate, 3.7%, was below its male rate, 4.3%). R explains A: high urban and youth unemployment pushes AP's overall rate above India's.

A: Animal husbandry is a genetic industry.
x: Both are true (it is not an extractive industry). R explains A: genetic industries breed plants and animals, which is what animal husbandry does.

A: The Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules do not automatically transfer subjects to Panchayats and Municipalities.
x: Both are true. R explains A: Articles 243G and 243W say the State Legislature 'may' devolve the 29 and 18 subjects, so transfer depends on State law.

A: The number of Padma Shri awards announced in 2026 was the same as in 2025.
R: The fall in total Padma Awards from 139 in 2025 to 131 in 2026 came wholly from fewer Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan awards.
x: Both are true: 113 Padma Shri in both years, while Vibhushan fell 7 to 5 and Bhushan 19 to 13. R explains A: the whole drop of eight lay in the higher awards.

A: Sachin Tendulkar's UN role in 2026 relates to road safety.
R: On 24 February 2026 Sachin Tendulkar was appointed the UN Global Road Safety Champion.
x: Both are true (he is not a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador). R explains A: his appointment as UN Global Road Safety Champion is the road-safety role.

A: Mars appears red because of iron oxide on its surface.
R: The Martian surface dust and rocks are rich in iron oxide (rust), which gives a reddish tint.
x: Both are true (the colour is not due to sulphates like gypsum). R explains A: rust-coloured iron oxide in the dust makes the planet look red.

A: The 1992 UN Principles on Nuclear Power Sources in Outer Space are not legally binding.
R: The 1992 Principles were adopted through UNGA Resolution 47/68, and General Assembly resolutions are only recommendatory.
x: Both are true. R explains A: being a General Assembly resolution, not a treaty, the Principles do not bind States.

A: Maharashtra's 2026 Bill to move the leopard from Schedule I to Schedule II of the Wildlife (Protection) Act needs the President's assent.
x: Both are true (the proposal was Schedule I to II, not II to I). R explains A: a State Bill amending the central WPA needs the President's assent.

A: Ghantasala, called Kantakossyla by Ptolemy, was a port of the Satavahana age.
x: Both are true (Kantakossyla is Ghantasala, not Koddura). R explains A: Ghantasala and Koddura were Satavahana ports of Indo-Roman trade.

A: The Kakatiyas were the second dynasty, after the Satavahanas, to unite all the Telugu lands.
x: Both are true (the Satavahanas were first). R explains A: Ganapatideva brought the whole Telugu area, from Ganjam to Kanchi, under one rule.

A: The Godavari delta is sinking relative to the sea.
R: Land subsidence in the Godavari delta exceeds the regional sea-level rise.
x: Both are true (the delta is not rising). R explains A: the land sinks faster than the sea rises, so the delta loses height relative to the sea.

A: The All-India Muslim League, formed in 1906, supported the partition of Bengal.
x: Both are true (it did not oppose the partition). R explains A: the early League was loyal to the British and kept away from the Congress-led anti-partition agitation.

A: Hepatitis D infects only people who also have Hepatitis B.
R: The Hepatitis D virus is incomplete and needs the Hepatitis B virus to replicate.
x: Both are true (HDV spreads through blood and body fluids, not the faecal-oral route). R explains A: without HBV the D virus cannot multiply.

A: A bleached coral is not necessarily dead.
R: Bleaching is the loss of zooxanthellae under stress, and corals can recover them if the stress ends.
x: Both are true. R explains A: bleaching only means the algae and pigment are lost, so the coral can survive and recover.

A: Under Union Budget 2026-27, old MAT credit set-off is not available to every company whichever tax regime it chooses.
x: Both are true. R explains A: set-off of old MAT credit is allowed only to companies moving to the new regime, capped at one-fourth.

A: A Biosphere Reserve is not a protected-area category under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the WPA categories are only National Park, Wildlife Sanctuary, Conservation Reserve and Community Reserve.

A: Tikkana helped restore Manumasiddhi II to the Nellore throne.
R: Tikkana went as envoy to Kakatiya Ganapatideva, who sent forces to reinstate Manumasiddhi II.
x: Both are true (Tikkana served Manumasiddhi II, not Manumasiddhi I). R explains A: his embassy won Kakatiya help that restored Manumasiddhi II.

A: Sati was practised in Vijayanagara.
x: Both are true (Abdur Razzaq is not among those who describe it). R explains A: Nuniz, Conti and Barbosa record the practice in Vijayanagara.

A: Planting coastal shelterbelts and mangroves is a pre-disaster cyclone mitigation measure.
R: Coastal vegetation acts as a buffer that reduces wind speed and storm-surge damage.
x: Both are true (removing coastal trees increases, not reduces, risk). R explains A: vegetation buffers blunt the cyclone's wind and surge.

A: The Tana Bhagat movement (1914) was a movement of the Oraons led by Jatra Bhagat.
R: Jatra Oraon of Ranchi district began the Tana Bhagat movement against landlords, taxes and evil social practices.
x: Both are true (Govind Guru led the Bhils' Bhagat movement, which ended at Mangarh in 1913). R explains A: Jatra Oraon's leadership among the Oraons was the Tana Bhagat movement.

A: Hydropower output falls during droughts and years of low snowpack.
R: Hydropower depends on river flow, which drought and low snowmelt reduce.
x: Both are true (hydropower is not unaffected). R explains A: less water in the rivers means less power generated.

A: The Jains of Potlacheruvu were persecuted by the Kalamukhas and Virashaivas in the Kakatiya age.
R: The Kakatiyas turned to Shaivism from Prola II and Rudradeva, after which Jain–Saiva conflicts grew.
x: Both are true: the persecution came in the Kakatiya age, not the Eastern Chalukya period. R explains A: the Shaiva turn under the Kakatiyas set Kalamukhas and Virashaivas against Jain centres like Potlacheruvu.

A: Mughal karkhanas mainly produced luxury goods for the royal household.
R: The karkhanas were imperial workshops run by the Mir Saman (Khan-i-Saman) to meet the needs of the court.
x: Both are true (they did not mainly produce bulk grain for the army). R explains A: as workshops serving the court, they made fine goods for the royal household.

A: India was due to host the Quad Leaders' Summit after the 2024 summit.
R: Hosting of the Quad leaders' summit rotates among the members, and the US hosted the 2024 summit at Wilmington.
x: Both are true (the 2025 summit due in India was not held). R explains A: after the US, it was India's turn to host.

A: A caste-like stratification is found among Indian Muslims too.
x: Both are true (recent inter-caste conflicts are mostly over land, wages and power, not ritual status). R explains A: the Ashraf, Ajlaf and Arzal categories are such a stratification.

A: Revenue from the auction of mineral blocks accrues to the State Governments.
R: Under the MMDR Act the States own the minerals in their territory and conduct the auctions of mineral blocks.
x: Both are true (the revenue does not go to the Union). R explains A: the States, as owners and auctioning authorities, receive the auction premium.

A: Rock phosphate cannot be applied efficiently through fertigation.
x: Both are true. R explains A: fertigation applies only fertilisers dissolved in irrigation water, and rock phosphate is insoluble.

A: The Ashvamedha of Vasishthiputra Santamula is attested by an altar found at Nagarjunakonda.
x: Both are true (the altar is at Nagarjunakonda, not Amaravati). R explains A: Santamula performed the Ashvamedha, Vajapeya and Agnistoma, and the altar is the physical trace.

A: In a well blowout, oil or gas escapes uncontrollably from the well.
x: Both are true (the Sivasagar blowout of 12 June 2025 was controlled by 21 June, not in two months). R explains A: the escape happens when well pressure overcomes the preventers and drilling mud.

A: CyberKnife is used to treat tumours with radiation.
x: Both are true (it treats, not maps, tumours). R explains A: CyberKnife is a robotic, image-guided system delivering a precise radiation dose.

A: Gwalior fell to the rebels in 1858 though the Scindia stayed loyal to the British.
x: Both are true (the Scindia did not join the revolt). R explains A: his troops went over to the Rani of Jhansi, so Gwalior fell despite his loyalty.

A: The five Zonal Councils are chaired by the Union Home Minister.
R: Under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, the Union Home Minister is the common chairman of all the Zonal Councils.
x: Both are true (the Prime Minister does not chair them). R explains A: the SRA makes the Home Minister chairman of each council.

A: The Economic Survey 2025-26 favours trust-based compliance over inspection-based enforcement.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Survey's shift from 'regulation and control' to 'enabling' means trusting firms instead of inspecting them.

A: Kala-azar is spread by the sandfly.
R: Kala-azar is caused by Leishmania donovani, transmitted by the bite of female Phlebotomus sandflies.
x: Both are true (Anopheles spreads malaria, not kala-azar). R explains A: the sandfly is the vector of the parasite.

A: The Arya Samaj satyagraha in Hyderabad State was held in 1938-39.
x: Both are true (it was not in 1948). R explains A: the satyagraha was launched against the Nizam's curbs on religious and civil rights.

A: National Road Safety Month 2026 was observed in January 2026.
R: Road Safety Month is observed from 1 to 31 January, enclosing the National Road Safety Week of 11-17 January.
x: Both are true (it was not in February). R explains A: the Month is fixed for January every year.

A: The Bashir Bagh firing of 28 August 2000 took place during the agitation against electricity tariff hikes.
x: Both are true (it was not during the Bhu Poratam). R explains A: Left parties and farmers were protesting against tariff hikes under power-sector reforms.

A: Asset monetisation does not transfer ownership of brownfield public assets to private players.
x: Both are true. R explains A: assets are only leased for a fixed period, so ownership stays with the government.

A: Shivaji recaptured most, but not all, of the forts ceded at Purandar.
x: Both are true. R explains A: after escaping from Agra he won back most of them, such as Purandar, Lohagarh and Mahuli.

A: The Dravida temple style is marked by a pyramidal vimana.
R: The Dravida tower rises in storeys (talas) that diminish upward.
x: Both are true (the curvilinear shikhara belongs to the Nagara style). R explains A: the stepped storeys give the vimana its pyramidal shape.

A: The Governor cannot pardon a sentence passed by a court martial.
x: Both are true (that power is the President's under Article 72). R explains A: the Governor's power under Article 161 covers only offences against laws on State executive matters.

A: After 1813 British manufactured goods flooded the Indian market.
x: Both are true (Indian textiles were taxed in Britain, not admitted free). R explains A: the Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's monopoly and opened Indian trade to all British merchants.

A: A hurricane is a warm-core system.
R: A hurricane draws its energy from latent heat released as moisture from warm ocean water condenses in its core.
x: Both are true (a hurricane is not cold-core). R explains A: the heat released in the core keeps it warmer than its surroundings.

A: The Planning Commission was a non-constitutional body.
x: Both are true. R explains A: it was created on 15 March 1950 by a Cabinet resolution, not by the Constitution.

A: Mutnuri Krishna Rao is best remembered as the editor of Krishna Patrika.
x: Both are true (he did not found it). R explains A: as editor he made Krishna Patrika a political weekly and a hub for freedom fighters.

A: PMMSY focuses on fisheries infrastructure and the value chain.
x: Both are true (it does not rely mainly on fleet expansion). R explains A: PMMSY is a long-term infrastructure and value-chain scheme.

A: The 14th Finance Commission raised the States' share to 42% without separate treatment for Special Category States.
x: Both are true (the 42% applied to all States, not only Special Category States). R explains A: the 14th FC made no distinction between general and Special Category States.

A: Climate change affects species migration.
x: Both are true. R explains A: rising temperatures shift species ranges, forcing them to migrate.

A: Rare-earth elements are not geologically rare.
x: Both are true. R explains A: their rarity is economic and technological, as they are hard to separate, not a matter of crustal scarcity.

A: Betting and gambling are subjects in the State List of the Seventh Schedule.
R: Entry 34 of the State List covers betting and gambling.
x: Both are true (they are not in the Union List). R explains A: Entry 34 of List II places them with the States.

A: The UDHR is not legally binding on UN member States.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the UDHR is a declaration adopted by a General Assembly resolution, not a treaty.

A: Many deep-space probes generate their power from radioactive decay rather than solar panels.
x: Both are true (they do not carry fission reactors). R explains A: RTGs turn the heat of radioactive decay into electricity, useful far from the Sun.

A: Oceanic clines inhibit vertical mixing of water.
R: A cline separates lighter surface water from denser water below, and this stable layering resists mixing.
x: Both are true (clines do not promote mixing). R explains A: the sharp density contrast across a thermocline or halocline blocks vertical exchange.

A: The name Rayalaseema was adopted at the Andhra Mahasabha held at Nandyal in 1928.
x: Both are true: the session was at Nandyal (November 1928), not Kurnool. R explains A: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao proposed the name there.

A: Samprati was the grandson of Ashoka.
R: Samprati was the son of Kunala, a son of Ashoka.
x: Both are true (he was not Ashoka's son). R explains A: as Kunala's son, Samprati was Ashoka's grandson.

A: The Rampa rebellion of 1922-24 was not the first rising of the region's hill tribes.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Koyas had risen several times before, e.g. in 1803, 1840 and 1858, and there was a Rampa rebellion in 1879.

A: The Dancing Girl of Mohenjodaro is a bronze figure.
R: The Dancing Girl was cast by the lost-wax technique.
x: Both are true (the Harappa male torso is red sandstone, not bronze). R explains A: lost-wax casting is the method by which the bronze figure was made.

A: The Dutch factory at Machilipatnam (1605) was the first European factory in Andhra.
x: Both are true (the English factory of 1611 came later). R explains A: the Dutch set up at Machilipatnam in 1605 under Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, before any other European power.

A: Rice was a major crop of the Kakatiya period.
x: Both are true (maize was not a Kakatiya crop; it came later from the Americas). R explains A: even a fragrant rice variety was grown near Orugallu.

A: Chennai port is an artificial harbour.
R: Chennai lies on a straight east coast with no natural shelter, so its harbour had to be built.
x: Both are true (it is the oldest artificial port, 1881, but not the deepest - Visakhapatnam is). R explains A: lacking a natural harbour, Chennai needed an artificial one.

A: Sugarcane is one of the most water-intensive crops of India.
x: Both are true (it is not water-efficient). R explains A: sugarcane needs about 1,400-2,300 mm of water in the sub-tropics and 2,000-3,500 mm in the tropics.

A: Vizianagaram came under the East India Company's control after the battle of Padmanabham (1794).
x: Both are true. R explains A: Raja Vijayarama Raju was killed fighting the Company at Padmanabham, ending the Pusapatis' resistance.

A: As per ICRIER's "The Participation Paradox", a rural woman now earns less than half of a rural man's earnings.
R: A rural woman's earnings have fallen to about 45% of a rural man's, from about 53% earlier.
x: Both are true (she does not earn more than half). R explains A: 45% is below one half.

A: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla is the first Indian astronaut to reach the International Space Station.
R: Shukla flew to the ISS on the Axiom-4 mission in June 2025, while Rakesh Sharma's 1984 flight went to the Soviet Salyut-7 station.
x: Both are true (Rakesh Sharma was the first Indian in space). R explains A: Sharma never visited the ISS, so Shukla is the first Indian to reach it.

A: Rayalaseema is one of the main drought-prone regions of India.
R: Rayalaseema gets low and erratic rainfall, lying in the rain shadow region.
x: Both are true (Lower Assam is a high-rainfall flood zone, not drought-prone). R explains A: scanty, unreliable rain makes Rayalaseema drought-prone.

A: In the Early Green Revolution phase (1968-81), HYV seeds were introduced first in wheat.
R: The first HYVs adopted were the Mexican dwarf wheat varieties of Norman Borlaug, grown mainly in Punjab, Haryana and western UP.
x: Both are true (rice came later). R explains A: the Green Revolution began with Borlaug's dwarf wheat.

A: Harappa was not a port of the Harappan Civilisation.
x: Both are true (Lothal was the chief port). R explains A: Harappa was an inland city on the Ravi.

A: A 22-year-old is not disqualified on grounds of age from being a member of a municipality.
x: Both are true. R explains A: Article 243V fixes the minimum age at 21, so a 22-year-old qualifies.

A: Unlike Ashoka and Kanishka, Pushyamitra Sunga is described in Buddhist texts as a persecutor of Buddhism.
R: The Divyavadana says Pushyamitra destroyed monasteries and offered rewards for the heads of monks.
x: Both are true (he did not help spread Buddhism). R explains A: the Divyavadana account is the basis of his image as a persecutor.

A: Plant varieties cannot be patented in India.
R: Section 3(j) of the Patents Act, 1970 excludes plants and plant varieties, which are protected instead under the PPV&FR Act, 2001.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Patents Act excludes plant varieties from patentability.

A: Under the post-26/11 three-tier coastal security arrangement, the Coast Guard is not responsible for shallow waters.
x: Both are true (shallow waters are the State Marine Police's). R explains A: the Navy has overall responsibility and the Coast Guard covers territorial waters.

A: The Sutlej rises outside Indian territory.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Sutlej rises at Rakas Tal in Tibet and enters India at Shipki La.

A: Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself at Kilokhri in 1290.
R: The Turkish nobles and people of Delhi distrusted the new Khalji ruler, so he stayed at Kilokhri instead of entering the city.
x: Both are true: the coronation was at Kilokhri, not Badaun. R explains A: Delhi's hostility kept him at Kilokhri.

A: AP FiberNet offers households internet, cable TV and phone services over one connection.
x: Both are true (the Fibergrid was inaugurated by President Ram Nath Kovind, not the Prime Minister). R explains A: AP State FiberNet offers triple-play services.

A: Ujjawala (2007) is an anti-trafficking scheme.
x: Both are true (PM Ujjwala Yojana, 2016, gives LPG connections). R explains A: Ujjawala dealt with prevention of trafficking and rescue and rehabilitation of victims.

A: The elected members of a State Legislative Assembly do not take part in the election of the Vice-President.
R: The Vice-President is elected by the members of both Houses of Parliament only (Article 66).
x: Both are true. R explains A: the electoral college for the Vice-President has no State legislators.

A: Bihar became the first State to offer mobile e-voting in its urban local body polls (June 2025).
R: Its C-DAC app 'e-Voting SECBHR' let voters vote by phone, using blockchain and face-matching.
x: Both are true (the app ran on Android, not only iOS). R explains A: the app is what made mobile voting possible.

A: An astronaut in an orbiting satellite feels weightless.
x: Both are true (mass never becomes zero). R explains A: craft and astronaut fall with the same acceleration, so the normal force, the felt weight, is zero.

A: The Rashtriya Gokul Mission does not cover exotic breeds such as Jersey.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Mission focuses on indigenous cattle and buffaloes.

A: KABIL has acquired five lithium blocks in Argentina.
R: KABIL was formed to acquire critical and strategic mineral assets, such as lithium, abroad.
x: Both are true (the blocks are in Argentina's Catamarca, not Chile). R explains A: securing overseas lithium is KABIL's purpose.

A: The AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026 makes Amaravati the sole capital with effect from 2 June 2024.
R: The Act amends Section 5 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, which had made Hyderabad the common capital only until 2 June 2024.
x: Both are true (the date is 2 June 2024, not 2014). R explains A: the common-capital period ended on that date, so the amendment makes Amaravati the sole capital from then.

A: Vijayanagara temples were built largely of local granite.
x: Both are true (the 'Athens of Vijayanagara' was the valley around the Virupaksha temple, not Hazara Rama). R explains A: the Deccan plateau gave easy access to granite.

A: India is chairing the Kimberley Process in 2026.
R: The Kimberley Process chair rotates every year, and India took over on 1 January 2026 for the third time.
x: Both are true (the Process has no headquarters at New Delhi). R explains A: India holds the rotating chair for 2026.

A: The UNFCCC entered into force in 1994.
R: The UNFCCC was adopted in 1992 at Rio and entered into force 90 days after the 50th ratification.
x: Both are true (it was adopted, not brought into force, in 1992). R explains A: the 50th ratification came in 1993, so it entered into force on 21 March 1994.

A: Gujarat has India's second largest mangrove cover (ISFR 2023).
R: Only West Bengal, with the Sundarbans, has more mangrove cover than Gujarat.
x: Both are true (AP is not second). R explains A: with West Bengal first, Gujarat comes second.

A: The White Revolution in India drew on the Anand cooperative model of Gujarat.
x: Both are true (it began in Gujarat, not Punjab). R explains A: Operation Flood built a national milk grid on the Anand (Amul) three-tier model.

A: The targets of NPIT 2012, such as 10 million more trained ICT workers, were to be achieved by 2020.
x: Both are true (the year is 2020, not 2025). R explains A: NPIT 2012 aimed to make India the global IT-ITES hub by 2020.

A: The PSLV-C62 mission (12 January 2026) lost EOS-N1 'Anvesha' along with 15 co-passenger satellites.
R: A roll-rate disturbance at the end of its third stage made the mission fail.
x: Both are true (the first stage did ignite). R explains A: the third-stage failure caused the loss of all the satellites.

A: Large UAVs such as Heron, Predator and Reaper run on fuel-powered engines.
R: Long-endurance flights need the high energy density of fuel, which batteries cannot match.
x: Both are true (they do not run on batteries). R explains A: fuel lets these drones stay aloft for many hours.

A: IN-SPACe is the regulator and promoter of private space activity, not ISRO's commercial arm.
x: Both are true (NSIL is ISRO's commercial arm). R explains A: IN-SPACe (2020, Ahmedabad) is the single-window regulator of the space sector.

A: The Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought is awarded by the European Parliament.
R: The European Parliament set up the prize in 1988 in honour of Andrei Sakharov.
x: Both are true (it is not given by the Norwegian Nobel Committee). R explains A: it is the European Parliament's own prize.

A: In Andhra Pradesh, MPTC and ZPTC elections are held on party symbols.
R: Only Gram Panchayat (Sarpanch and ward) elections in Andhra Pradesh are held without party symbols.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the non-party rule applies only to Gram Panchayats, so MPTC and ZPTC polls use party symbols.

A: India INX at GIFT City is regulated by IFSCA, not SEBI.
x: Both are true. R explains A: exchanges in the International Financial Services Centre are regulated by IFSCA.

A: India is called the 'pharmacy of the world'.
x: Both are true (India is third, not second, by volume). R explains A: India supplies medicines to more than 200 countries.

A: The Polavaram Project Authority was constituted by the Government of India.
x: Both are true (not by the AP Government). R explains A: Polavaram is a national project under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, and the Centre set up the PPA to handle its funding and coordination.

A: A writ petition under Article 32 cannot be filed for the violation of an ordinary legal right.
x: Both are true. R explains A: Article 32 can be invoked only for the violation of fundamental rights.

A: The natural rate of unemployment excludes cyclical unemployment.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the natural rate is made up only of frictional and structural unemployment.

A: B.C. Dutt took part in the Royal Indian Navy revolt of 1946.
x: Both are true (he was not an INA officer tried at the Red Fort). R explains A: he was a rating of the RIN in 1946.

A: Iraq is not a member of the Gulf Cooperation Council.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the GCC has only six members - UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Qatar and Kuwait.

A: A State Human Rights Commission cannot punish those who violate human rights.
x: Both are true. R explains A: an SHRC can only recommend compensation or action to the Government.

A: The first Vijayanagara-Bahmani war was fought in the reign of Bukka I.
x: Both are true (not Harihara I). R explains A: the first war was fought by Bukka I against Muhammad Shah I (1362-67).

A: Monetary tightening by major central banks can lead to capital outflows from India.
R: Higher interest rates abroad make foreign assets more attractive to investors than Indian ones.
x: Both are true. R explains A: when returns rise abroad, foreign investors pull money out of India, one of the spillovers of global tightening.

A: Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep are not members of the Southern Zonal Council.
R: Andaman and Nicobar and Lakshadweep are not members of any Zonal Council and are only special invitees to the Southern Zonal Council.
x: Both are true (the Southern Council has AP, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Telangana and Puducherry). R explains A: the two island UTs attend only as special invitees.

A: The operator of a fire-and-forget missile such as Nag need not keep tracking the target after launch.
x: Both are true. R explains A: a fire-and-forget missile guides itself after launch, so the operator is free.

A: Free Trade Zones were set up in India mainly to promote exports.
x: Both are true (not mainly to develop backward areas). R explains A: duty-free landing, processing and re-export make FTZs export platforms.

A: In-situ conservation means conservation within the natural habitat.
R: In-situ conservation protects species where they occur, through national parks, sanctuaries and biosphere reserves.
x: Both are true (conservation outside the habitat is ex-situ). R explains A: in-situ protects species in their own habitat.

A: YSR Sampoorna Poshana Plus is implemented in the 77 tribal mandals of Andhra Pradesh.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the plain Sampoorna Poshana covers the non-tribal mandals, so the Plus version serves the 77 tribal mandals.

A: The SACRED portal is meant to connect senior citizens with jobs.
R: SACRED (Senior Able Citizens for Re-Employment in Dignity) links job providers with senior citizens who wish to work.
x: Both are true (it is not a health insurance portal). R explains A: SACRED is a re-employment platform for the elderly.

A: Varavikrayam is a social drama.
x: Both are true (it is not a padya natakam). R explains A: social dramas like Varavikrayam, against the dowry evil, presented contemporary evils in spoken Telugu prose.

A: Gandhi returned to India in 1915 on the advice of Gopal Krishna Gokhale.
R: Gokhale, whom Gandhi regarded as his political guru, urged him to come back and serve India.
x: Both are true (it was Gokhale, not Tilak). R explains A: Gandhi returned at his political guru's urging.

A: Tribal society, unlike peasant society, has little market-linked individual landholding.
x: Both are true. R explains A: tribal society is relatively isolated, kinship-based and egalitarian, unlike market-linked peasant society.

A: The RBI has played a developmental role in building India's financial institutions.
R: The RBI helped set up IDBI, NABARD and NHB as part of its developmental role.
x: Both are true (EXIM Bank was set up under an Act of Parliament, not by the RBI). R explains A: these institutions came from the RBI's developmental work.

A: Virasam (1970) is not the Telugu counterpart of the All India Progressive Writers' Association.
x: Both are true (Virasam is the Revolutionary Writers' Association). R explains A: Arasam (1943) was the Telugu counterpart of the AIPWA.

A: The Indian Famine Code of 1883 was prepared from the report of the Strachey Commission.
x: Both are true (the Lyall Commission came later, in 1897). R explains A: the Strachey Commission, appointed in 1878 after the Great Famine, reported in 1880 and led to the Code.

A: Communication satellites are used to relay TV programmes all over the world.
x: Both are true (ground waves cannot do this). R explains A: three geostationary satellites can together cover nearly the whole globe.

A: When a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject conflict, the Union law does not always prevail.
x: Both are true. R explains A: under Article 254(2) a State law reserved for and assented to by the President prevails in that State.

A: Finance Commission grants to local bodies can be held back when local body elections are not held.
x: Both are true (AP's local bodies were run by special officers, not the SEC). R explains A: the grants require elected bodies, audited accounts and SFC compliance.

A: Parent material is one of the factors of soil formation.
x: Both are true (soil colour is a property, not a factor). R explains A: limestone giving calcium-rich soil shows parent material shaping soil.

A: Red sanders is a tree of the dry deciduous forests of the Seshachalam hills.
R: Red sanders is endemic to the dry southern Eastern Ghats - the Seshachalam, Palakonda and Veligonda ranges.
x: Both are true (it is not a tropical rainforest tree). R explains A: its native range is the dry deciduous belt of these hills.

A: The Telangana Armed Struggle did not end with the Police Action of September 1948.
R: The Communists continued the armed struggle against the Indian Union until they withdrew it in October 1951.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the struggle went on until 1951, well after the Police Action.

A: The Mahayana Buddhism of the Kushana age used Sanskrit.
R: Mahayana texts of the age, such as the works of Ashvaghosha, were composed in Sanskrit.
x: Both are true (Pali-Prakrit was the language of early Buddhism). R explains A: its major texts were in Sanskrit.

A: Under the Golden Rule of public finance, the government may borrow only to finance capital expenditure.
x: Both are true (salaries and pensions are revenue spending). R explains A: capital expenditure creates assets that repay the borrowing.

A: YSR Cheyutha had no ₹10,000 income condition for applicants.
R: Eligibility for YSR Cheyutha rested on being a BC, SC, ST or minority woman aged 45-60 residing in Andhra Pradesh.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the criteria were community, age and residence, not a ₹10,000 income cap.

A: Nagavasu Naidu Sunkara won a silver medal in 5 km racewalking at the World Transplant Games 2025.
R: He competed in the organ recipient category, having had a liver transplant in 2020 with his mother as the donor.
x: Both are true (it was silver in racewalking, not gold in cycling). R explains A: his liver transplant made him eligible for the Games.

A: Rural-to-urban migration explains most of the gap between urban and rural population growth.
x: Both are true (natural increase does not). R explains A: natural increase is similar in rural and urban areas, so migration accounts for the gap.

A: The International Day of Cooperatives has no fixed calendar date.
x: Both are true (it is not always 4 July). R explains A: it is observed on the first Saturday of July.

A: Andhra Pradesh was not given a numerical first rank in BRAP 2020.
x: Both are true. R explains A: BRAP 2020 placed States in categories such as 'top achievers' rather than numerical ranks.

A: The Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification scheme approved on 13 May 2026 has not been withdrawn.
R: Although no bidders have come so far, the scheme's bid windows have been kept open.
x: Both are true. R explains A: keeping the bid windows open means the scheme continues.

A: India's National Action Plan on Climate Change gives importance to adaptation.
x: Both are true (the updated NDC did not remove adaptation). R explains A: four of the NAPCC's eight missions focus on adaptation.

A: Rock bolting and wire mesh are structural landslide-mitigation measures.
R: Rock bolting and wire mesh physically stabilise the slope.
x: Both are true (hazard mapping and early warning are the non-structural ones). R explains A: they are physical works on the slope.

A: Patna Bird Sanctuary, designated on World Wetlands Day 2026, is a Ramsar site of Uttar Pradesh.
x: Both are true (it is not in Bihar). R explains A: Patna Bird Sanctuary is in Etah district of Uttar Pradesh.

A: The Supreme Court's opinion on a Presidential reference under Article 143 is not binding on the President.
x: Both are true. R explains A: an Article 143 reference yields only an advisory opinion.

A: Seshachalam is the only biosphere reserve of Andhra Pradesh.
R: Andhra Pradesh has one tiger reserve (Nagarjunasagar–Srisailam), one elephant reserve and one biosphere reserve, the last being Seshachalam.
x: Both are true (NSTR is a tiger reserve, not a biosphere reserve). R explains A: the State's single biosphere reserve is Seshachalam.

A: Jainism declined under the Kakatiyas from the reign of Rudradeva.
R: The Kakatiyas turned Shaiva from Prola II and Rudradeva, after which Kalamukha and Virashaiva hostility to the Jains grew.
x: Both are true (it did not flourish unchallenged). R explains A: the Shaiva turn and Jain–Saiva conflicts caused the decline.

A: The Purna Swaraj resolution was passed by the Congress at its Lahore session of 1929.
R: The Calcutta session of 1928 gave the British one year to grant Dominion Status, failing which the Congress would demand complete independence.
x: Both are true (not Calcutta 1928). R explains A: when the one-year deadline lapsed, the Lahore session of 1929 adopted Purna Swaraj.

A: Temples of the mature Vesara (Gadag) style of the Kalyani Chalukyas carry fine, detailed carving.
x: Both are true (their star-shaped plans became a Hoysala model, not a Kakatiya one). R explains A: soft chloritic schist (soapstone) allowed intricate carving.

A: Andhra Pradesh's Population Management Policy (2026) shifts the focus from population control to managing ageing and the demographic dividend.
R: Fertility in Andhra Pradesh has fallen below the replacement level, and its population is ageing.
x: Both are true (the policy is not stricter population control). R explains A: with TFR about 1.5, controlling numbers is no longer the problem.

A: The Damodar does not rise at Amarkantak.
R: Amarkantak is the source of the Narmada and the Son, while the Damodar rises in the Chota Nagpur plateau of Jharkhand.
x: Both are true. R explains A: Amarkantak gives rise to other rivers; the Damodar's source is in Chota Nagpur.

A: Wurtzite boron nitride is not accepted as the hardest naturally occurring substance.
R: Its claimed greater hardness than diamond rests only on simulations, so diamond remains the accepted hardest natural substance.
x: Both are true. R explains A: a simulation result is not accepted fact.

A: The systems model of public policy was given by David Easton.
R: Easton saw public policy as the output of the political system responding to inputs from its environment.
x: Both are true (Thomas Dye is not its author). R explains A: Easton's input-output view of the political system is the systems model.

A: The National Makhana Board is located in Bihar.
R: Bihar produces most of India's makhana (fox nut).
x: Both are true (not Telangana). R explains A: the Board is placed in the State that grows most of the crop.

A: The Sankosh is an international river.
R: The Sankosh rises in northern Bhutan and flows into India to join the Brahmaputra.
x: Both are true. R explains A: rising in Bhutan and flowing into India, the Sankosh crosses an international border.

R: Ram Lal dismissed NTR's government while it still had a majority, which NTR proved when he was restored a month later.
x: Both are true. R explains A: dismissing a government that still had a majority is why the episode is cited as a misuse of the Governor's discretion.

R: India's previous best at the event was 17 medals at Kobe 2024.
x: Both are true. R explains A: 22 medals beat the earlier best of 17, making New Delhi 2025 India's best-ever haul.

A: The Chandela ruler Vidyadhara attacked the Pratihara king Rajyapala.
R: Rajyapala had surrendered Kannauj to Mahmud of Ghazni without a fight in 1018.
x: Both are true. R explains A: Vidyadhara punished Rajyapala for his cowardly surrender of Kannauj to Mahmud.

R: Interest payments and pensions are committed expenditure that cannot be cut in the short run.
x: Both are true. R explains A: committed spending leaves little room to change the budget, which is fiscal rigidity.

R: USOF was created to fund telecom access in rural and remote areas where operators would not invest on their own.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the fund existed for unviable rural areas, which is why it was set up as a dedicated, non-lapsable fund.

R: Horticultural crops such as vegetables and fruits give far higher output per hectare than foodgrains.
x: Both are true (2024-25: horticulture 367.72 MT, foodgrains 357.73 MT). R explains A: much higher yields per hectare let horticulture out-produce foodgrains on less land.

R: Under Make in India and the PLI scheme, domestic manufacturing has replaced most mobile phone imports.
x: Both are true. R explains A: domestic production under these schemes is why nearly all phones used in India are made in India.

R: Rajasthan has high solar insolation and vast arid land for solar parks such as Bhadla.
x: Both are true. R explains A: abundant sunshine and land explain Rajasthan's lead in solar capacity.

R: Collecting and processing the quarter's data takes about two months.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the time needed to compile the quarter's data causes the two-month lag.

R: Only members of a House can vote in it, and a Rajya Sabha member is not a member of the Lok Sabha.
x: Both are true. R explains A: not being a Lok Sabha member, such a Prime Minister cannot vote there.

A: Padma Awards are not titles and cannot be used as a prefix or suffix to a name.
R: Article 18 abolishes titles, and the Supreme Court (Balaji Raghavan, 1995) upheld the awards only as honours that are not titles.
x: Both are true. R explains A: because Article 18 bars titles, the awards cannot be used with a name.

R: After the US revoked the Chabahar waiver in September 2025, only a six-month waiver (October 2025 – April 2026) followed, and it was not renewed.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the last short waiver lapsed in 2026, ending the exemption.

R: Andhra Pradesh's urban share (29.47%) was below that of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and Telangana.
x: Both are true. R explains A: with the lowest urban share, AP was the least urbanised southern State.

A: IBSAMAR is a trilateral naval exercise.
R: IBSAMAR brings together the navies of India, Brazil and South Africa, the IBSA countries.
x: Both are true. R explains A: three navies take part, so it is trilateral.

R: Alauddin Khalji needed to maintain a large standing army on fixed, low salaries against the Mongol threat.
x: Both are true. R explains A: market control kept prices low so the army could live on its pay.

R: Article 88 gives the Attorney General the right to speak in and take part in the proceedings of either House, without a vote.
x: Both are true. R explains A: Article 88 gives this right of participation.

R: The First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966) had recommended a Lokpal and Lokayuktas.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the 1968 Bill followed the ARC's recommendation.

A: Polavaram is executed with Union funding.
R: Polavaram was declared a national project under Section 90 of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
x: Both are true. R explains A: as a national project, the Union bears its cost.

R: Zafar Khan charged the Mongols under Qutlugh Khwaja without support from the Sultan's main army.
x: Both are true. R explains A: isolated in his charge, Zafar Khan was cut off and killed.

R: When r exceeds g, interest costs make debt grow faster than GDP unless offset by a primary surplus.
x: Both are true. R explains A: only a primary surplus can offset the gap between r and g and keep the ratio stable.

R: The Mughals had broken their oaths of safe passage given to the Guru on his leaving Anandpur.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Zafarnama rebukes Aurangzeb for this broken promise.

R: Vijayanagara temples carried the Dravida features of gopuras, vimanas and pillared mandapas to their most elaborate form.
x: Both are true. R explains A: this elaboration of Dravida features is why Percy Brown called it the matured Dravidian state.

R: Factories draw workers from villages to towns, creating urban centres.
x: Both are true. R explains A: industrial jobs pull migrants into towns, driving urbanisation.

R: Malala was 19 when she was designated, younger than any earlier Messenger of Peace.
x: Both are true. R explains A: her age at designation makes her the youngest ever.

R: Geostationary communication satellites are first placed in GTO and then raised to geostationary orbit by their own motors.
x: Both are true. R explains A: as a geostationary communication satellite, GSAT-30 was launched into GTO.

R: Section 4 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 establishes the FSSAI.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the Act's provision creates the Authority.

R: The Virashaivas rejected Brahmanical ritual and caste-based social rules.
x: Both are true. R explains A: rejecting Brahmanical norms led them to allow post-puberty marriage and widow remarriage.

R: The 2025 Act set only a minimum of two non-Muslim members, so the Court fixed an upper limit to keep them a minority on the Board.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the cap of three filled the gap left by the Act's minimum-only rule.

R: Velugu's federated SHG structure for poor rural women proved successful and was adopted by the Union for NRLM (2011).
x: Both are true. R explains A: NRLM copied Velugu's proven model.

R: Ambedkar held that nobody holds a patent right in the fundamental ideas of a constitution.
x: Both are true. R explains A: since no one owns constitutional ideas, borrowing them needed no apology.

R: Phosphorus is often the limiting nutrient for algae in fresh water, so an excess triggers algal blooms.
x: Both are true. R explains A: extra phosphorus removes the limit on algal growth, causing eutrophication.

R: C-DOT is the telecom research and development centre of the Department of Telecommunications.
x: Both are true. R explains A: as DoT's R&D arm, C-DOT developed the system for the Ministry.

R: The Lucknow Pact (1916) and the joint Khilafat–Non-Cooperation movement (1919-22) brought the Congress and the League together.
x: Both are true. R explains A: these two events mark the 1916-22 high point of unity.

R: Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib was built at the spot in Chandni Chowk where the Guru was beheaded.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the gurdwara marks the site of the execution.

R: Finland's innovation fund Sitra drew up the roadmap in 2016 as a national plan for a circular economy.
x: Both are true. R explains A: Sitra's 2016 national roadmap was the first of its kind.

R: The National Health Authority is an attached office of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.
x: Both are true. R explains A: as an office of the Health Ministry, it is governed by a Board under the Union Health Minister.

R: Forced acid ingestion causes the same kind of disabling injury that the RPwD Act's 'acid attack victim' category covers.
x: Both are true (recognised by the Supreme Court on 5 May 2026). R explains A: the injury fits the existing disability category.

R: Total reservation in local bodies must stay within the Supreme Court's 50 per cent ceiling, which left only 24.15 per cent for BCs after the SC and ST shares.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the 50 per cent cap forced the cut in the BC share.

R: Cordite is a smokeless propellant made of nitroglycerine and nitrocellulose.
x: Both are true. R explains A: nitroglycerine is one of its two main components.

R: The Act regulates rather than bans prenatal diagnostic techniques, allowing them for medical purposes while prohibiting sex determination.
x: Both are true. R explains A: medical uses such as detecting genetic abnormalities are allowed under its regulation.

R: Maharatna status is given to larger CPSEs with the aim of making them global giants.
x: Both are true. R explains A: larger firms with global ambitions get more autonomy than Navratnas.

R: The Koyna earthquake occurred close to the Shivajisagar reservoir, whose water load and seepage stressed the faults below.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the reservoir's effect on faults is reservoir-induced seismicity.

R: India signed the Artemis Accords during PM Modi's state visit to the US in June 2023.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the signing came during that visit.

R: South India saw less Persian influence, so its music kept its devotional temple roots.
x: Both are true. R explains A: with little Persian influence, Carnatic music stayed tied to Bhakti.

R: Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah built the Charminar in 1591 to commemorate the end of a plague in his new city.
x: Both are true. R explains A: it was built to mark the end of the plague.

R: Female literacy in most districts, especially in Rayalaseema and north coastal Andhra, lagged well behind the national average.
x: Both are true. R explains A: with most districts below the national level, only three districts exceeded it.

R: In a dense crowd, pressure on the chest prevents breathing.
x: Both are true. R explains A: compression that stops breathing is compressive asphyxia.

R: The Committee felt that the unity, security and economic prosperity of the country after Partition should come first.
x: Both are true. R explains A: putting national unity first led it to reject linguistic states at first.

R: Ibrahim Qutb Shah spent years in exile at Vijayanagara, learnt Telugu and patronised Telugu poets, who gave him the Telugu name.
x: Both are true. R explains A: his Telugu patronage earned him the Telugu name Malkibharama.

R: Andhra Pradesh's candidate sites, such as the Lepakshi temple, are only on UNESCO's tentative list.
x: Both are true. R explains A: none of AP's sites is yet inscribed.

R: Andhra Pradesh, the lower riparian State, fears these upstream projects will cut its share of Godavari and Krishna waters.
x: Both are true. R explains A: AP objects as the lower riparian State.

R: The Central Information Commission hears second appeals and complaints under Sections 18 and 19 of the RTI Act.
x: Both are true. R explains A: AppCOMS 2.0 digitises the CIC's appeals and complaints work.

R: When the RBI sells securities, banks pay for them out of their reserves, which reduces liquidity.
x: Both are true. R explains A: payment from bank reserves drains liquidity.

R: Customs Union members adopt one tariff towards non-members, while FTA members keep their own external tariffs.
x: Both are true. R explains A: a common tariff is a Customs Union feature, not an FTA one.

R: Electrolysis splits water into hydrogen and oxygen, and using renewable power makes the process carbon-free.
x: Both are true. R explains A: carbon-free electrolysis is what makes hydrogen 'green'.

R: PESA extends Part IX Panchayats to the Fifth Schedule Areas and empowers Gram Sabhas, without creating legislative bodies.
x: Both are true. R explains A: PESA works through panchayats and Gram Sabhas, not legislatures.

R: The Gupta period saw great achievements in literature, art, science and mathematics.
x: Both are true. R explains A: these achievements earn the period the title Golden Age.

R: Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), whose rural sanitation outcomes the survey assesses, is run by the Ministry of Jal Shakti's Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation.
x: Both are true. R explains A: the ministry that runs SBM-G conducts its survey.

R: Bhagat Singh and Dutt wanted only to 'make the deaf hear', not to kill, and they courted arrest.
x: Both are true. R explains A: their aim of protest, not killing, is why the bombs were harmless.
